_note: NOT MERGEABLE: merge/annotate refuse MenuSelectionHandler.asm (transforms artifact, OQ-59). Corrected notes prepared for I024 and kept here for the decision in OQ-I024-1. Comment texts avoid the three transform patterns of this block.

blockNote: Choice-menu cursor for the dialog option op (COP #BE, cop_handlers_dialog.DialogueOptions, its only caller; 92 script sites) (Bank 03).

A on entry (read from the script as one 16-bit word): low byte = packed layout, high byte = first text row. Packed byte: low nibble C = items in the first column, high nibble N = total items when there are two columns; N = 0 means a single column of C items. Values seen in scripts: $02 (69 sites; first rows 0-3), $04, $03, $01, $32 (2 + 1 items), $42 (2 + 2), $63 (3 + 3).

Stack frame in the handler: SP+1/2 = selection (0-based, starts at 0), SP+3 = packed byte, SP+4 = first row, then the saved X and D. Inside DrawMenuCursor every offset is 2 higher (JSR return address).

Polls joypadCurrent once per frame (DrawMenuCursor, WaitOneFrame) against the mask $CF00: Up $0800, Down $0400, Left or Right $0300, confirm $8000 (the A button after the remap), cancel $4000 (the B button after the remap). Start is not accepted, and 'L/R' means the D-pad. Priority: Up, Down, Left/Right, confirm, cancel. The nav/action bits are then written into joypadHeld (the consumption word); that is not what 'suppresses auto-repeat': DialogueOptions sets joypadMaskInv = $0F00, which makes the D-pad bits repeat. db-us/transforms.json rewrites the three vanilla button constants in this block, so comments here use the post-transform values.
- Up: previous item; from item 0 it wraps to the LAST item of the second column (or of the only column), and from the top of column 2 it goes to the bottom of column 1 (not symmetric with Down).
- Down: next item inside the current column; wraps to the top of the SAME column.
- Left and Right do the same thing: toggle the column (index + C when that item exists, index - C from the second column); the sound plays only when the column changed.
- Sound effects go to sfxQueueCh2: navigation $10, confirm $11.

DrawMenuCursor writes two tiles (top $212C or $21AC, bottom $213C or $21AC) into the BG3 tilemap staging buffer (bg3TilemapBuffer, bg3TilemapRow1 = next row) at ((((first row + row in column) x 2 + $0980) x 32 + $097E) x 2) bytes plus the column offset ($18 bytes = 12 tiles for column 2), where $097E/$0980 are the dialog box origin. Bit 4 of the blink counter $0994 chooses the tile pair, so the cursor is lit for 16 frames and dim for 16 (32-frame period). The tiles under the cursor are saved in $0990/$0992 (position $098E) and restored before the cursor moves. displayModeFlags bit 0 is set on every redraw (consumer not traced).

Returns A = 1-based selection with carry set; cancel returns A = 0. Y is clobbered (the parameter word is popped into it); X and D are restored. Confirm leaves the highlighted cursor drawn (the saved tiles are only cleared, not restored); cancel restores them through ReadMenuSelection first. The initial selection is always 0.

MenuSelectionHandler: Entry point. Pushes D, X and the parameter word, zeroes D, starts the selection at 0 with a cleared blink counter and loops in MenuSelection_PollLoop: draw the cursor, wait one frame, read joypadCurrent, dispatch on the first matching bit (Up, Down, Left/Right, confirm, cancel). Returns A = 1-based selection (0 = cancelled) with carry set. See the block note.
MenuSelection_Down: Down handler. Plays the navigation sound, resets the blink counter, unpacks C and N from SP+3 and advances the selection inside its column: in column 1 it wraps from C-1 to 0, in column 2 from N-1 back to C.
MenuSelection_LeftRight: Left/Right handler (both buttons act identically). Column 1: index + C if that item exists (below N), otherwise unchanged. Column 2: index - C. The navigation sound plays only when the column actually changed.
DrawMenuCursor: Draws the blinking two-tile cursor. Increments the blink counter $0994 (bit 4 chooses the lit pair $212C/$213C or the dim pair $21AC/$21AC), restores the tiles saved at the previous cursor position, computes the new tilemap offset from the first row, the row inside the column, the dialog box origin ($097E/$0980) and the column offset ($18 bytes for column 2), saves the two tiles now under the cursor in $0990/$0992 and writes the cursor tiles. Sets displayModeFlags bit 0. Parameter offsets are 2 higher than in the handler because of the JSR.
ReadMenuSelection: Cancel path: puts the saved tiles back into the BG3 buffer, stores (tile and $03FF) x 8 + $6000 for each of the two tiles in $090E/$0910 (the VRAM word address of that glyph in the font at $6000; not an OAM value, and no code reads $090E/$0910 in the extracted asm), clears $0990/$0992 and sets displayModeFlags bit 0.
